chance_note: Chance = a placebo: a second random-walk draw plays 'real' through the same model and the same 10462 Q1 cells (all-label and resolved-only), BH with every other real p; it passed 42, scaled to 13857 cells = the figure above. Nominal p<0.05 would give 693 of 13857 by chance; observed 2532.
intro: 13,857 cells across 160 barrier shapes (stop 0.25-2σ, target 0.5-3× the stop, 15 min to 21:00, fade and follow) and 55 conditions (class, London time, Lesson 05 regime, σ terciles, year, 34 instruments). 1,289 pass BH at q=0.10. A placebo (a second random walk playing 'real') passes 42 of 10,462 cells, about 55 when scaled to the whole sweep.

On the stage 2 question, 'will it hit the target first', no condition clears the random walk in a way that matters. 164 cells sit above it and 293 below. Small barriers with long clocks are about 0.01-0.025 AUC above; big barriers with short clocks are 0.02-0.18 below. Both come from the random walk mis-modelling time-outs (real vol arrives in bursts), not from the market picking a side.

Split the label, and one thing holds across every condition. Among touches that hit target or stop, the model does sort which side wins on symmetric 1:1 barriers, where a random walk is exactly 50/50. AUC is 0.517-0.58 against the random walk's 0.50. The gap is above 0 in 36 of 36 pooled cells, 94% of class cells, 93% of years, 97% of regime cells and 32 of 34 instruments. None of the 1:1 cells passes BH below 0.

It is a plateau, not a peak. At 0.5σ 1:1 2h the gap is +0.039, and every stop size and horizon from 0.25σ to 1σ sits above 0. Gold, GBPNZD and USDCAD are strongest; NZDCAD and EURCHF sit near 0. The weakest London bucket is NY afternoon. Turbulent regimes are a little stronger (+0.057), but they rest on 103 episodes.

Lesson 06 (net, bid/ask path) is where it stops. At equal 50% retention, the 'which side' top half beats the plain geometry top half by +0.017 to +0.055 R per trade at 0.25σ: 25 books pass BH as better and 4 as worse. The usual target-first meta filter does worse than geometry (5 better, 19 worse). Every book still loses: 1:1 0.25σ 2h fade is −0.165 R unfiltered, −0.151 with the direction filter and −0.168 with the geometry filter. The best net anywhere is −0.015 R, and the filters leave effective bets near 30 of 34.

Among vol-state features, only forecast error (F5) adds more on real labels than on the random walk: 27 BH passes, none below, up to +0.028 AUC on FX crosses at 0.25σ. σ level, σ over-reaction (F3), expected change, P(high vol), yesterday's jump and the dollar share add about nothing. Vol so far today and a jump earlier today add less on real labels than on a random walk (41 and 130 cells below), because intraday vol persists less than a random walk run at the realised vol.

Lesson 01 lag: with the session inputs delayed one more session, the 'which side' AUC on 1:1 0.25σ 2h keeps 0.511 of its 0.518. With every input delayed (intraday ones too) it falls to 0.503. The effect is not a session-alignment artefact, and most of it sits in same-session inputs.

Rule A's own trades (922, 2020-08-24 to 2022-12-12, +0.20 R net, Sharpe 1.54) are too noisy to tell. Meta AUC is 0.508 against 0.491 for shuffled labels (p 0.31), and keeping the top half cuts the Sharpe to 0.61 against 1.13 for a random half. Meta-labelling Rule A on this sample does not help.
